messages.author: e1b933a0d5bbe14f
messages.subject: appending files in Windows 8
parts:
I'm running what should be a straight-forward script on R running on Windows 8, but I keep hitting problems when I write the data to a file. The end of the script looks more or less like this:

cat(file='file.csv',output.column.names)
for(x in 1:length(output.data)){
cat(file='file.csv',output.data[x],sep='\n',append=T)
}

The problem is not just that I keep getting 'Permission denied' errors that crash the script, but that it crashes at different places. Sometimes it outputs some 300 lines before the error occurs. Other times x exceeds 1000. But it's always a different number.

So here's the workaround. To get it to work, I have to add:
for(delay in 1:300000){
}
before the looped cat command. Apparently R tries to access the file to write before the OS has really closed it. The 300,000 is the result of several trial-and-error runs.

So I got it to work, but I'm curious if anyone knows a better way to deal with this rather ridiculous problem. (Other than running R in Linux as I usually do.)

--
Kevin Parent, Ph.D
Korea Maritime University

messages.author: 97ce067823027f53
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] appending files in Windows 8
parts:
Kevin, 

I still don't understand why you are opening and closing the I/O connection on every element. It may be too much for the OS, but it seems quite inefficient -- or in R parlance it's not vectorized. Open it once with a connection or try write.csv, it should be much faster and do what you want. 

> dat <- rnorm(1e5)
> system.time({ for (i in 1:length(dat)) cat(file='file.csv', dat[i],sep='\n',append=T)})
   user  system elapsed 
 13.652  10.753  79.496 
> system.time({ write.csv(dat, file='file2.csv')})  # write to a different file
   user  system elapsed 
  0.305   0.013   0.321

> The fact that I stumped Stefan is strangely comforting. :-)
:-) I know nearly nothing about Windows 8 and from what I've seen I'm determined to keep it that way ;-)

Cheers,
STG
